subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted external-workspace agent-config discovery, or keep agent registration explicit and improve existing runtime management instead?
rationale: The request adds filesystem scanning, a public config surface, routing/session semantics, and security boundaries that cleanup automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Use `agents.list`, `$include`, `openclaw agents add`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, then improve docs or operator tooling without adding core glob discovery.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Define a core discovery contract with trusted roots, allowed filenames, validation, precedence, reload behavior, agentDir/session isolation, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Zero-Restart Management
options.body: Improve explicit runtime registration and binding reload semantics first, then revisit whether workspace glob discovery belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Use `agents.list`, `$include`, `openclaw agents add`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, then improve docs or operator tooling without adding core glob discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the model-visible `agents_list` discovery surface and current central agent-scope config paths.
